challenge.better_approach: Looked: ALTER ... REFRESH alone silences the warning but leaves indexes sorted under the old glibc order, which can corrupt text-keyed lookups; REINDEX first is postgres's own documented fix, so this is the smallest correct recipe.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the 2.39->2.43 glibc change altered no collation order the indexes rely on in a way REINDEX cannot repair; REINDEX rebuilds from the heap, so it holds. Also that sudo -u postgres works for the postgres-owned databases (passwordless sudo since 11-11).
challenge.prior_art: Consulted intentions-congruency-lab, intentions-not-beside-code and tickets for 'collation': no hit. Outline 11.3.5 names postgres a host service Recovery upgrades; nothing in it covers collation.
challenge.real_collision: None: 3ef8654a8027 (remote db sync) touches the same db but not its host config; Recovery (6.3.5) owns upgrades in the outline, and this intention is the recipe it will run, not a rival.

answers.falsifier: the verify exits 0 on akienasus after apply, and exits non-zero on a box whose recorded collation version still differs
answers.how: A host-seam intention in intentions-not-beside-code carrying an apply (per database whose datcollversion differs from pg_database_collation_actual_version: REINDEX DATABASE then ALTER DATABASE <db> REFRESH COLLATION VERSION, as its owner) and a verify (no database's recorded version differs from the actual one, and a psql connect to cairn prints no mismatch warning). Apply on akienasus now.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (an error is loud at a diagnostic surface, so a standing warning on every connect is noise that buries real ones) and outline 11.3.5 (postgres is a host service, upgraded by Recovery); the host-seam class: the seed must carry what an upgraded box needs.
answers.what: After an OS upgrade moves glibc, every postgres database on the box has its indexes rebuilt and its collation version refreshed, so no connect warns of a collation version mismatch.

bullets.text: the mismatch is on cairn, postgres AND template1, so a database created after the upgrade inherits the stale version from template1; the apply covers all three
Recovery (6.3.5) has no upgrade step yet that would run this after a release upgrade; the horizon names the trigger, nothing fires it
